I'll carefully compare the source and draft, hunting for signature losses.

**Key observations:**

1. The opening command and "marble sepulchre" line — present, well-preserved.
2. "The vast white headless phantom" → draft drops "vast" but keeps the phrase shape — minor.
3. "Beneath the unclouded and mild azure sky, upon the fair face of the pleasant sea, wafted by the joyous breezes" — draft compresses to "Beneath the mild azure sky upon the pleasant sea" — loses "unclouded," "fair face of the pleasant sea," and crucially "wafted by the joyous breezes." This ironic contrast (joyous breezes/great mass of death) is voice-critical and interpretively weighted.
4. The italicization of "_shoals, rocks, and breakers hereabouts: beware!_" — lost in draft (no italics). This is a textual distinctiveness marker.
5. "There's a most doleful and most mocking funeral!" paragraph — fully preserved.
6. The "There's orthodoxy!" rhetoric — fully preserved.
7. Final ghost paragraph and Cock-Lane closing — fully preserved.

The "joyous breezes" / "fair face of the pleasant sea" / "unclouded" passage is the ironic contrast that makes "great mass of death floats on and on" land with full force. Its compression flattens Melville's deliberate tonal irony.

The italic log entry is a textual signature (the only italicized direct inscription in the chapter), and dropping the italics erases its rhetorical distinctiveness.
